findings.claim: The requirement now names three page identities (memorycard_revision, source_revision beside source, legacy engram_revision) but does not say what happens when a page carries more than one, or which wins. Readers could disagree on the revision adopted for a page with conflicting fields. The adjacent scenario says only 'under its page identity' and does not define identity precedence or conflict handling.

The inline '(Previously: ...)' changelog note is embedded in normative requirement text. It will go stale as history and does not belong in a living spec; a SHALL requirement should state only current behavior.

The refusal scenario was loosened to 'revision (under its page identity) is missing, non-numeric or negative'. It no longer covers a page that carries none of the three identities, which the removed 'engram_revision' wording and the old 'page of any other identity was refused' behavior addressed. Whether such a page is refused for the revision or for identity is now unspecified.

evidence: Single-file spec change; only the revision-reading requirement and one scenario GIVEN were edited.
No code changed, so no runtime regression is possible from this diff; findings concern spec precision only.
